content.text:
Two of your posts compare a CPU service against an NVIDIA L4. Both use EmbeddingGemma 2 on Cloud Run:

1. **EmbeddingGemma 2 on Cloud Run: an int8 CPU Service Against an NVIDIA L4** (published 2026-10-13)
   https://dev.to/gde/embeddinggemma-2-on-cloud-run-an-int8-cpu-service-against-an-nvidia-l4-15ac
   Its description says it deploys EmbeddingGemma 2 on a 1 vCPU instance with an int8 repack and on an NVIDIA L4, with tests, a semantic search demo, benchmarks and a cost per million documents.

2. **EmbeddingGemma 2 on Cloud Run: Minimum Specs, and When an NVIDIA L4 Pays for Itself** (published 2026-10-15)
   https://dev.to/gde/embeddinggemma-2-on-cloud-run-minimum-specs-and-when-an-nvidia-l4-pays-for-itself-5c1k
   Its description says it finds the smallest Cloud Run instance the model fits in and tests whether an int4 repack shrinks it further. It also works out how many documents a burst needs before an NVIDIA L4 costs less than a 1 vCPU int8 service.

To find these I searched the index for "CPU" in the title or description and "L4" in the title, description or body. That search returned only the first post. I added the second because its description names the 1 vCPU int8 service and the L4. I matched on titles and descriptions only and did not read the article bodies.

About 35 other posts mention both "CPU" and "L4" in the body. Their titles and descriptions show GPU deployments, so I left them out. One of them, **The Cheapest CUDA GPU on AWS Has an Arm CPU — and You Probably Want the Intel One** (https://dev.to/aws-builders/the-cheapest-cuda-gpu-on-aws-has-an-arm-cpu-and-you-probably-want-the-intel-one-325b), is about the host CPU on two GPU instances with the same Turing GPU, not a CPU service.
